title: Ross Jenkins on email, SMS and WhatsApp marketing, freelancing on Upwork, and avoiding common marketing mistakes
summary: Ross Jenkins, CEO of DigitalME, explains how his agency uses email, SMS and WhatsApp marketing, how he built his business through Upwork, and how identity-resolution retargeting works for e-commerce. He also shares his pricing approach and the top mistakes he sees business owners make.

principles.text: Stick to the channels you can deliver best results in, rather than offering every marketing service.
principles.quote: I want to kind of stick to stick to what works and stick to what we can build like the best performance

principles.text: Drop service lines where you can't be the best, even if they were once part of your business.
principles.quote: we're amazing the emails we get great results so what's the point in being in another space that we're not going to be the best at

principles.text: Always add upsells to your site and sales flow; it's one of the biggest, most overlooked marketing wins, especially in B2C.
principles.quote: upselling probably the second biggest thing you know why haven't you got upselling on your website I don't understand especially in your BTC it makes complete sense

principles.text: Know your audience in detail and build a persona, then test different ways to reach it rather than trusting generic marketer advice.
principles.quote: understand every part of your audience and what they're doing um and build it build a Persona and then Market to it

principles.text: Price fixed-scope projects at roughly 20% over your hourly estimate to cover slow payers and scope leeway.
principles.quote: I quote 20% over what I believe it will be in terms of my hourly and then just do it that way

principles.text: Make buying as easy as possible for the customer, since people pay a premium for convenience.
principles.quote: you want to make it as easy as possible for a client to purchase
